interactions.title: Azogar and Murook board and inspect the airship
lines: DM: She kind of looks at Azogar walking with his cane, and scrambles. She quickly climbs up the rope ladder and greets you all acknowledging the previous meeting with Delwath, Riswynn, Wellby and Kenzo, who's like off doing some meditating, or something, and sort of gives a nod to Seeker, and says, “You must be the other dwarf.”
DM: Do you have an easier way to ascend the ship? I am afraid the Loremaster no longer has the strength to climb this ladder.

((Checking whether Kenzo can inspect the visitors))

Seeker: Well, I mean these- I I look around and make eye contact meaningfully like these Rainbow orcs. I haven't spent time with them, but you have. They're our friends, right? I'm saying implicitly. ((Kenzo is elsewhere))Well, Seeker just sort of nods to himself like, I'll just. I'll just be a little careful about it. I won't. I won't spill all the beans. But also won't be able to resist showing off. So.

Seeker: We walk over to the not hidden or anything portion of the ship that has the the whole apparatus, which is, yeah, the phasing stone, an egg-shaped crystal stone surrounded by a- I'm trying to remember. There's like a metal gold and silver lattice work around it, and it's on stone pillars with that. So I think here's the heart of the operation. It's the the the stone that bears the magical power, and I'm as we refer to it attuned to it. So it is connected to my mind.

Seeker: And if you'll just hold on to the side rail, if you would. He like braces himself slightly. I can, for example, make the ship rise briefly, and I just- we just ascend a few. Give him a sense of acceleration.

Seeker: A powerful wizard. We— Thank you. We do have a great deal of assistance. We work together in these matters, many contributions from within our group here, and from others as well. We we have powerful allies.

interactions.title: Azogar shares uncertain lore of crystallized planar magic
lines: DM: Fascinating, fascinating, and and what is that magical stone called?

DM: I have not heard more of such things. There are sometimes tales that have come to us of phase stones that are associated with the Feywild, crystallized magic they're called. Is that what you're talking about here?
Riswynn: Well, we'd heard that your cloak was associated with the Feywild. I think a lot of tales bring Feywild into any sort of magic or wondrous object.
DM: He kind of glances over at Murook at when you say that. Where did you hear such a tale?
Delwath: Where did we hear the tale about the rainbow cloak coming from the Feywild?
Seeker: Oh, this is from my- my mentor, a dwarven scholar.
DM: A dwarven scholar's discussing the lore of the Feywild, and—
DM: And our cloak. Interesting. The the history of— Hmm. I did not think that history of the cloak was widely known.
Seeker: It it may or may not, I shall not say more just yet.
DM: Sometimes we Loremasters are prone to—

Seeker: I consider myself a bit of a loremaster as well. Seeker's demeanor has sort of slightly changed as we start talking about history of things, and he's been shuffling around and pulling out my books, thumbing through.
Seeker: But actually, this idea of the the phase—
Seeker: And that is an intriguing notion. I had wondered myself what the name that we'd heard of the stone might refer to, with respect to phasing.

Riswynn: Lore and understanding are valuable things, and we encourage these matters of discourse. But there is an army bearing down on us. Perhaps we should talk more about catapults and boiling oil and dropping stones.

Seeker: There's time time enough for that, of course, of course, but but the— I I would be interested to know from this unique individual what— Stories of these stones of the fey he he might have, and and yours you might exchange.
DM: Yes, I would I would be happy to tell you the lore of our people about these stones.

DM: It is said— Well, there are many tales, and sorting the truth of these tales from the rumors that spread, especially among people who have been so scattered for as long as ours, is not always straightforward, and it has taken me many years to try to corroborate tales and rumors from story to story. But certainly, I think you are right, Seeker, and I would be fascinated to discuss this further with you, because it seems that each shard of crystal magic has its own resonance with some other place that is not of this world.

Seeker: Seeker's fiercely scribbling and cross-referencing: resonance with a particular place. That matches some intuitions I've had for for a while, but it is a a more precise articulation of the concept. And what evidence do you have from your—
DM: I have. I have no magic myself, and I've never been able to test any of these hypotheses. I am sadly reduced to being in this matter, and my duties keep me far more— And—
DM: ((Audio interruption))so I so I have never— it has been simply a a hobby of mine, I must say, to try and understand these tales.

DM: As you know, or or maybe you have not heard those stories yet, for many, many years our people wandered, separated and lost across the world, and traveled quite widely in that time. Always hiding and never staying in one place for very long. Because, of course, the ever-present danger of being hunted kept us from settling.
Seeker: These are the people of the cloak of the rainbow or Orcs generally?
DM: These are these are us. These are my people, our people.

DM: But many histories were collected in that time, and rumors passed in story, and very little is written. So I've had to spend years asking the elders and the villages across Xurkhaz, what their grandparents told them and what their grandparents' grandparents told us.

DM: It seems that there are tales of in wild places in the world far from civilization, finding crystallized magic, the matter that captured the elemental essence of these extraplanar regions that are associated with fire and water and air.

DM: It is said a tale has come down to us of a hero of our people from dozens of generations ago, who supposedly used this crystallized water essence to create fog and hide his people for years and years and years and years.
Seeker: The essence of water or of ice?
DM: Oh, I I don't know about ice. I think this was water.

DM: But the story was that all sorts of planar energy could be captured and and resonate with these phase stones. And so I am fascinated to know what plane, what energy your phase stone resonates with.

Seeker: To be honest, we are still getting to know its capabilities. And I have been actively studying it, as we learn how to maneuver the ship. But practical concerns have overridden, as they do sometimes.

before: Seeker: Yes, we may not be able to provide another magical ship, but we're willing to see how we can use ours to help you.

Seeker: Oh, but that's probably not blocked by—
Delwath: Well, I don't know. We don't know.

Seeker: I see, the— that is the transition point. It's where it's where you—

interactions.title: Lubash explains the barrier and his brother’s death
lines: DM: What would you like to know?

Delwath: I forget. What's her name? Murdoch, or Maruk? Murook? Your General Murook seemed uncertain as to what the dangers would be to your troops and your armies from Grash's ring, and his ability to raise orcs from the dead.

DM: You must understand the nature of the power I bear and the nature of our chained brethren.

DM: The chains, the fires, if severed suddenly, without proper care, without a ritual of support and without the right attitude in the— In the severed chained one. It will drive most of our chained brethren mad.

DM: There is little of them, for there is little independent thought in their minds that is not the will of Thark, and without that will, they are not fearsome in battle. And when they cross the river Thark's voice will fail.
DM: But if this Grash creature can raise them unchained under his control, well, that is a different story, and one that indeed scares me.
DM: If they are still driven by the will of Thark, they are of no concern to me. They will not defeat our armies.

DM: And I have carried on his wishes, pacing—
DM: Fell in battle. Hill giants came across the borders, raiding or seeking food. While he was traveling on one of his tours to maintain the barriers that keep Thark silent within our borders.
